title: Pelagic AI - Private Link & Region Gating Discovery
summary: Intro call to validate Pelagic AI's private deployment requirements: VPC peering options, PrivateLink vs Private Endpoints, regional gating for EU data residency, and security controls (KMS, SSO, audit logs). Determined next steps: exchange network checklist, schedule architecture deep-dive, run small egress test in eu-west-1, and provide indicative pricing for Dedicated reserved pool.

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-11-03
- Time: 15:00 PT / 23:00 UTC
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Nikhil (Redwood SE), Ruth (Pelagic Head of Platform), Arjun (Cloud Architect), Leah (InfoSec), Samir (SRE)

Auto-generated summary: Pelagic wants private deployment with strict EU gating, likely hybrid (some hosted for dev, private for prod). Main blockers: egress policy, customer-managed KMS, and corporate firewall constraints.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intros, we'll keep this loose — want to understand your constraints and then go into options for Private Link / peering.
[00:20] Ruth Jensen: Hi all, thanks. I'm Ruth, we run platform at Pelagic. We're evaluating Redwood for inference serving — mainly private mode. We need EU-only production, dev in hosted is ok for non-sensitive datasets.
[00:36] Arjun Patel: Arjun here, cloud architect. main concerns: cross region egress charges, private endpoints, DNS resolution inside our VPC — and how Redwood handles failover without routing data outside EU.
[00:50] Leah Moore: Leah, InfoSec. SOC 2 scope, SSO (SAML), customer-managed keys for model inputs, audit logs with 1 year retention, and a clean paper trail for model calls.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Great. Quick context from our side — Carlos will walk the architecture. High level: Redwood Private can run in your VPC via Private Endpoints/Privatelink (cloud vendor names may vary). We also offer Dedicated (reserved) pools in our accounts if you prefer we host but isolate.
[01:25] Carlos Alvarez: Hey. I'd like to sketch two patterns: 1) VPC peering/transit gateway: Redwood peered into your VPC or transit, we route through our data plane but you control egress; 2) PrivateLink/Privatelink endpoints: we expose an interface endpoint into your VPC so traffic never transits public internet. Both can be combined with regional constraints.
[01:50] (murmur) Samir Khatri: so PrivateLink keeps traffic internal, right?
[01:56] Carlos Alvarez: yeah, effectively—interface endpoints inside your VPC that hit Redwood's private endpoint in the same region. but caveat: some control-plane signals still go to Redwood control plane unless you run fully Private (we have a Private control plane option).
[02:12] Ruth Jensen: What's the Private control plane entail? Like, do we host it?
[02:18] Nikhil Rao: quick answer — Private control plane can be customer-facing: we run a control plane in your VPC or VPC peered environment, you keep audit logs and KMS keys. There's an on-prem package option if needed but that's a bigger SOW.
[02:34] Leah Moore: Do you support customer-managed KMS (CMK) in all deployment modes? We need HSM-backed keys ideally.
[02:41] Carlos Alvarez: yes, we integrate with cloud KMS and many HSM providers via standard APIs. for eu region we can hook to your CMK for at-rest model artifact encryption and optionally encrypt token payloads. Note: some roots are still in Redwood control plane unless Private control plane is requested.
[02:57] Arjun Patel: DNS — if we use interface endpoints, how do DNS entries look? We need internal domain names mapped to private IPs; can't have public cname leakage.
[03:08] Carlos Alvarez: we use split-horizon DNS in that scenario: we publish private hostnames within your VPC. occasionally the auto generated certs and names get munged by the transcript, but essentially we give you private FQDNs, and we can provide documentation for conditional forwarding.
[03:22] Ruth Jensen: good. region gating — if we have EU-only policy, how do you ensure model fallbacks don't call out to us-east-1?
[03:30] Maya Chen: we can pin routing policies per workspace. For example, pin your production workspace to eu-west-1 and fail closed or fallback to an EU model variant if capacity shortage occurs. We also support automated fallback policies but you can disable cross-region fallback.
[03:48] Leah Moore: Are fallback logs visible to us? We need immutable audit trails when requests are routed or failed over.
[03:55] Nikhil Rao: yes logs — we can ship request-level logs to your S3 or to your SIEM via our log delivery. retention and immutability settings are controllable, we can discuss retention windows.
[04:08] (brief pause)
[04:15] Arjun Patel: Two network constraints: our prod VPC is behind strict NACLs and we use a transit gateway. We prefer peering through transit gateway to keep a single egress posture. How would Redwood plug in?
[04:28] Carlos Alvarez: we can peer to your transit VPC or speak via inter-region peering. for transit gateway, it's usually a one-time configuration: attach Redwood's peered VPC and route the traffic. downside: more routing table entries; upside: simple for you.
[04:41] Ruth Jensen: latency — our SLO for inference is 150ms p95 internal. can Redwood meet that running eu-west-1 models with private endpoints?
[04:50] Maya Chen: depends on model size and batching. Basic distill models are trivial; large 8B+ models with kv cache warm-up can spike. Redwood Optimize recommends batching and kv cache warm pools. Carlos, want to add quant/throughput note?
[05:04] Carlos Alvarez: yeah. We can tune kernel selection and use quantized variants; for the same model, a quantized 4-bit variant often halves latency under same hardware. But quantization affects output quality and you'd want evals. We'll propose a perf/quality matrix for your dev/test prompts.
[05:20] Leah Moore: About credentials — we must use SAML SSO and RBAC on the admin console. Can you integrate with our IdP?
[05:27] Maya Chen: yes SAML SSO supported. RBAC we map to roles and can sync group membership. audit events appear per token and per user.
[05:34] Samir Khatri: Are there any ports we need to open outbound from our private subnets? Our security team hates surprises.
[05:40] Carlos Alvarez: for PrivateLink it's just traffic over the interface endpoint — no outbound 0.0.0.0 needs to be open. for peering, you'll need route to Redwood subnets and allow TCP 443 to our endpoints. we'll provide explicit CIDR ranges.
[05:55] (slight crosstalk)
[06:02] Ruth Jensen: about multi-region: we might want eu-west-1 primary and eu-central-1 standby for DR. if we failover, we need data residency controls and re-keying — is that possible?
[06:14] Nikhil Rao: possible — we keep workspace-level policies for region priorities. for re-keying, we can re-encrypt artifacts with the standby region's CMK but that does require orchestration. It's part of a DR runbook which we can include in the pilot SOW.
[06:29] Arjun Patel: networking — do you support AWS PrivateLink and Azure Private Endpoint both? We're multi-cloud internally.
[06:36] Carlos Alvarez: yes we support both, though implementation details differ (AWS interface endpoints vs Azure private endpoints). We often maintain a consistent abstraction in our control plane. sometimes the transcript mangles terms but the gist is the same.
[06:49] Leah Moore: Compliance question: will Redwood's Private deployment be in scope for SOC 2? We need attested controls for the components we rely on.
[06:58] Maya Chen: Redwood's hosted services are SOC 2 compliant. For Private deployments, our enterprise plan includes an extension for SOC 2 scoping guidance and we can provide a carve-out report showing which components are vendor-managed vs customer-managed. We'll share the compliance pack.
[07:12] Ruth Jensen: on connectivity costs — if we use PrivateLink, interface endpoint hourly costs plus data processing charges apply. Any guidance on cost delta between peering and PrivateLink?
[07:23] Carlos Alvarez: usually PrivateLink is slightly more predictable; peering/transit may incur cross-AZ/region data transfer costs depending on topology. We'll run a quick TCO calc for your expected throughput after we get your token volumes.
[07:36] Arjun Patel: token volumes: in prod we expect ~3M tokens/day to start, spiking 3x during batch jobs. dev is negligible.
[07:45] Maya Chen: good number — that helps sizing Dedicated pool vs pay-as-you-go. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and cost predictability; Private mode can be either Dedicated inside your VPC or Hosted Dedicated with VPC peering.
[07:58] (pause as someone shares a deck link)
[08:05] Ruth Jensen: shared doc: 'Pelagic - Redwood intake matrix' link (not pasted).
[08:10] Maya Chen: perfect. we'll pull that and align the network checklist to it.
[08:15] (interruption, keyboard sounds)
[08:22] Samir Khatri: small nit — does your runtime require GPUs in customer VPC or do you run on our bare metal?
[08:29] Carlos Alvarez: we support both. For mixed infra many customers use Redwood-managed GPU pools peered into their network. full on-prem and air-gapped installs are possible but usually require additional SOW and offline install media.
[08:43] Leah Moore: any telemetry we can't opt out of? We must ensure PII isn't flaked into debugging traces.
[08:51] Nikhil Rao: we can disable certain debug telemetry and filter logs. request-level payloads are never sent to third parties. there are redactions and pseudonymization features we can enable.
[09:03] Maya Chen: want to move toward next steps — action items we flagged. Carlos, can you outline the architecture deep-dive agenda?
[09:10] Carlos Alvarez: yes: 90-min deep-dive: 1) Network topology review and CIDR mapping, 2) PrivateLink vs Transit options and routing adjustments, 3) KMS/HSM integration and key rotation, 4) Failure modes and DR runbook, 5) Pilot scope and perf test plan.
[09:28] Ruth Jensen: works for us. prefer the deep-dive next week.
[09:32] Maya Chen: we'll propose two slots. Nikhil will run the small egress test in eu-west-1 to confirm connectivity and baseline latency.
[09:41] Arjun Patel: for the egress test, will you need firewall rules updated?
[09:45] Nikhil Rao: minimal — we'll use a short-lived interface endpoint; we'll send exact IPs and ports.
[09:51] Leah Moore: Regarding SSO/SAML configs we'll need an SP metadata file and someone to test the SAML flow.
[09:58] Maya Chen: we'll provide the metadata and a test plan.
[10:02] (brief silence)
[10:05] Ruth Jensen: one last question — licensing: if we do Dedicated reserved for 12 months, what's the commit? can we scale after pilot?
[10:13] Maya Chen: usual reserved tiers are monthly/annual. we can provide a flexible pilot SOW that converts to a committed Dedicated pool if you want. we'll put sample price ranges in the follow-up.
[10:23] (some agreement)
[10:30] Maya Chen: ok — recap quick: we'll send network checklist and security pack, propose deep-dive slots, run egress test, and prepare Dedicated estimate. any other blockers?
[10:40] Arjun Patel: none from my side.
[10:43] Leah Moore: none. thanks.
[10:46] Maya Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up by Friday.
[10:50] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-labels and some product names mangled (Privatelink vs PrivateLink vs private link). Speakers occasionally overlap. The transcript includes filler words and minor mis-hearings (e.g., 'kv cache' as 'key V cache').

Referenced artifacts: "Pelagic - Redwood intake matrix" (link shared in chat), Redwood Private deployment checklist (to be sent), compliance pack (SOC2 docs), sample SOW for pilot.

End of transcript.
